title: Test the boundary
summary: Return None for division by zero and test the ordinary and boundary cases.

scenario.briefing: A reporting function divides totals by counts. The empty case must return None instead of crashing the report.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Return None for the zero case.
Keep the ordinary division for everything else.

misconceptions.description: Catching every exception to hide failures.
misconceptions.feedback: Catch the specific failure you can handle. A broad catch hides programming errors.
None means absence. Coercing it to zero changes the meaning of the result.

sections.title: Python functions and collections
sections.body: Functions are defined with def and return values explicitly: def add(left, right): return left + right. Lists preserve order, dictionaries map keys to values, and comprehensions build a new collection from an iterable.

steps.title: Divide safely
steps.prompt: Edit report.py. safe_divide returns None when the divisor is zero and the quotient otherwise.

files.content:
def safe_divide(left, right):
    return left / right

steps.title: Testing boundaries

statements.label: Division by zero raises ZeroDivisionError in Python.
None is a deliberate absence value, not an error object.
A boundary test should include the zero divisor.
A test passes if the code merely runs without an exception.

steps.explanation: The boundary is the zero divisor. Returning None makes the absence explicit, and the test asserts both the boundary and ordinary cases.
